results.note: Drops the .lower() normalization, so an executable name differing only in case no longer matches the lowercase keys in EXE_RESUME/registry lookups.
None-vs-truthiness -- an empty-string resume cap (falsy but not None) now short-circuits as a hit instead of falling through to the executable-based lookup.
Comparison flip inverts the reopen-safety check, marking every declared-safe tool unsafe and every unclassified tool safe to reopen.
Guard flip in the platform-applicability check -- an os-scoped profile now applies unconditionally everywhere, while a platform-agnostic profile now never applies.
or->and swap lets a well-typed profile that simply doesn't apply on this platform slip through unrejected, silently promoting an inapplicable inject profile.
Inverts the core relaunch-safety guard, letting the tool relaunch into an already-open file -- the hidden-second-session data-loss scenario the function exists to prevent.
Inverts the consent check so injection proceeds when the user declines the prompt and is refused when they approve it.
Comparison flip on the finally-block safety net -- the pre-inject sidecar is restored only when the file is unchanged, never in the actual case where an unverified paint corrupted it.
Boolean flip inverts which branch handles a resumed+relaunch item -- routes to the injection flow only when discard was requested.
None-vs-truthiness -- a successful tool exit code of 0 is falsy, so it is no longer recorded into res.tool_exit after the injection flow.
Drops the reversal, breaking the documented 'LAST JSON line wins' contract -- now returns the first valid JSON line, which can be a stray warning printed before the real result.
None-vs-truthiness -- a driver result of {} (a valid but empty JSON object) is wrongly treated as 'no result line found' instead of proceeding to be filled in with ok/rc.
and->or swap lets a None value (which satisfies value != "") pass through, appending the literal string 'None' as a driver argument instead of being skipped.
